images.title: Cutting your product list down
images.alt: Four steps to fix promoting too many products: pick three to five, learn them properly, test for a drawback, write one comparison.
images.caption: A short list you know well beats a long list of links you can't explain.

items.title: Pick three to five products
items.text: Choose the ones that solve your audience's main problem.

items.title: Learn them properly
items.text: Use them, or read the docs, pricing page and forum complaints.

items.title: Run the drawback test
items.text: If you can't name one specific drawback from memory, don't recommend it yet.

items.title: Write one comparison
items.text: Finish one thorough comparison before adding anything new.

images.title: Traffic spikes vs search traffic
images.alt: Comparison of one-off traffic spikes, which are hard to repeat, with search traffic that keeps arriving from people close to buying.
images.caption: Treat a viral post as a bonus and put your effort into traffic that keeps coming.

columns.label: Traffic spikes
points: Volume can hide a page that converts badly

columns.label: Search traffic
points: Think "X vs Y" or "best X for..."
Start with terms a new site can rank for

images.after: 5. Writing for Google first and the reader second
images.title: Write for the reader first
images.alt: Checklist for reader-first articles: answer early, draft like explaining to a friend, use searcher words in headings, cut keyword-only sentences.
images.caption: A reader who has to dig for the answer leaves before reaching your recommendation.

items: Put the answer in the first few lines
Draft it the way you'd explain it to a friend who asked
Check that headings use the words a searcher would type
Rewrite any sentence that only exists to hold a keyword
Don't pad the article to hit a word count
